packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 19 - unverified image reading (first reader, images only)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this text before or during the reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-014 of this packet. I did nothing beyond the rules. I have not tried to identify the work or author.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001, image-004, image-008 and image-012 are reduced overviews with a ruler; the others are native-resolution tiles.
- The object is a narrow horizontal strip of parchment cut from a bifolium: the strip preserves about 20 short lines of each column, with the top and bottom lines cut through. A vertical gutter fold with sewing holes/slits is visible in image-004, image-007, image-008 and image-009.
- Language: Middle Dutch (Flemish/Brabantine spellings), in rhymed couplets, one verse per line. Small gothic book hand (textualis), brown ink, much abraded.
- Layout: two columns per page. The first letter of every verse is set apart in its own column to the left of the line. No rubrics, running titles, enlarged initials, underlining or glosses are visible in the surviving area.
- image-001 and image-012 show the strip folded so that one leaf lies over the other; at the edges of these views a line of the leaf underneath shows (noted below). image-004 and image-008 show the opened inner spread: two columns on the left leaf, the gutter, two columns on the right leaf.
- A horizontal fold/crease with tape repair runs through the middle of every column (about lines 9-12), where the writing is largely lost.
- In image-002 lines 12-13 are indented and without the set-off initial; a pencil "x" stands in the left margin beside line 4. Tentative interpretation: the indented lines are a scribal insertion or re-written lines; I cannot tell from the image.
- In image-014 line 10 a small letter (a?) stands at the right end of the line, and line 11 is crossed by a tear; I cannot tell whether line 11 is struck through.
- Names abbreviated: "co·" (coninc), "lod'" (Lodewijc?), "wybt·" (Wybert?).

SELECTED AREAS: all eight column-segments were read. Unread/failed: the crease lines in each column and the lower half of the fourth column of the inner spread (image-011), which is abraded and cut.

Conventions: the set-off initial is written joined to its line. ʒ = the -et/-at abbreviation (dʒ = dat, mʒ = met). A macron or ' marks an abbreviation stroke kept from the page; expansions in ( ). ? follows an uncertain reading.

=====================================================

LIMITATIONS
- Every column is cut at top and bottom, so no column gives continuous text beyond about 19 lines, and the order of the columns across the two leaves is not established by the images; I have not inferred it.
- The central crease, tape and abrasion remove two to four lines in the middle of every column.
- Column 1 of the inner spread has lost its initials at the trimmed left edge; column 4 is badly rubbed in its lower half.
- Many minims are ambiguous (n/u/m/in/ni); proper names (and'nakē, oestrike, brūeswich, sauoye, almaēgiē, cuelne, mes, triere, parijs, tulpin, wybert, gwide, morelāt) are read letter by letter and several are uncertain as marked.
- A wider or raking-light image of the crease zone, and a higher-resolution tile of the lower right column of image-011, would help.
- This is an unverified image reading.
